gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns the flux quantity A_j being incorrectly identified with the tangential exact-differential integral dφ instead of the normal derivative flux. ISSUE-001 concerns a different Cauchy/double-layer definition using |dξ| versus dξ; it does not diagnose the flux identity or its source/sink interpretation.

Both identify the incorrect sign in the quadratic term of f_G, the resulting wrong real part, and the false item (3) of the complex-layer lemma; the proposed sign correction is the same mathematical repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The displayed plus sign in f_G makes (z−z̄)^2 contribute a negative Im(z)^2 term, so Re f_G does not equal the stated Green function G and item (3) is false.

component_coverage.gold_component: The sign/algebra in the definition and real-part calculation of f_G is wrong, making item (3) of the complex-layer lemma false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly computes the negative quadratic contribution, states that the claimed representation does not reproduce G, and gives the correcting sign change.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false unweighted transpose relation D_s=D^T in the Nyström matrices, specifically because quadrature weights and operator/kernel structure prevent that identity. ISSUE-003 also calls for the explicitly defined D_s or the true weighted adjoint, covering the gold repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The adjoint/discrete matrix is not generally the ordinary transpose: the arc-length weights require a weighted-transpose relation, so using D_s=D^T misweights the operator on nonuniform discretizations.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed identity D_s=D^T is false because the matrix entries use different quadrature weights and normal/kernel arguments; the correct relation is weighted and affects implementation.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction compares D and D_s entries, identifies the differing weights and nonsymmetric dependence, rejects D_s=D^T, and directs use of the explicit or true weighted-adjoint matrix.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold concerns double application of quadrature weights in the singular S_1^k block and the resulting wrong product-quadrature scaling. ISSUE-003 concerns the separate D_s versus D^T matrix relation and does not diagnose the singular-kernel quadrature coefficient.

Both identify that the discrete Steklov pencil omits the mean term in S_0, so the constant-density/zero-mode subspace is mishandled and the stated full Steklov problem is not represented. ISSUE-004 also supplies the corresponding inclusion of the mean term or a consistent gauge fix.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed eigenproblem uses S(I−M) instead of the modified operator S(I−M)+M, causing constants to be annihilated rather than mapped to themselves and thereby losing or mishandling the zero Steklov mode and reconstruction guarantee.

component_coverage.gold_component: The discrete pencil omits the +M mean term from the right-hand operator, annihilates constant densities, and therefore fails to represent the full Steklov problem including the zero mode.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the continuous S_0 form, identifies the discrete omission of the mean term and its constant-shift problem, explains the reconstruction consequence, and proposes either a gauge fix or inclusion of the mean term.
